title: HydroCart Indoor Growing Tower
heading: HydroCart, an indoor growing tower from Abstraction Solutions.
text:
Home › HydroCart
HYDROCART
A six-plant hydroponic tower on a rolling cart, built to show what our AI can do. It watches its own water, pH and air, forecasts what comes next, and keeps the hands-on work to a few simple steps.
Build something like this See how the AI loop works

title: HydroCart Indoor Growing Tower
heading: What HydroCart is
text:
HydroCart is our showpiece, not a product for sale. It holds six plants in a small footprint and runs a nearly autonomous loop: sensors measure the system, our own AI model learns from those readings, and it predicts where each reading is heading so problems show up before they hurt the plants.
The same approach works for other equipment that needs watching, which is why we use it to show clients what a custom AI system can do.

title: HydroCart Indoor Growing Tower
heading: How the AI loop works
text:
Measure. An Arduino Mega reads pH, the water level in two tanks, and the temperature and humidity at two points on the cart.
Remember. It saves 10-minute averages on the board itself, enough for about 2.6 days of readings even with no computer attached.
Forecast. A Python app runs our AI model and predicts every reading 30 minutes, 6 hours and 24 hours ahead.

title: HydroCart Indoor Growing Tower
heading: How the AI loop works
text:
y reading 30 minutes, 6 hours and 24 hours ahead.
Check itself. Each forecast is scored against five simpler methods using rules we set before looking at the results, so we only trust the AI where it actually does better.
Show it. Live readings and forecasts appear on a dashboard, so the few hands-on steps happen at the right time instead of on a guess.

title: HydroCart Indoor Growing Tower
heading: What's on the cart
text:
A rolling cart with a fixed central tower holding six plants
A tote reservoir at the bottom, plus a backup tank up top
A small pump that carries the nutrient solution up the tower so it trickles back down past the roots
An aerator and a heater for the water
Grow lights
An Arduino Mega with pH, water-level, temperature and humidity sensors
Most of the cart is built from reused parts, with about $50 in new parts.

title: HydroCart Indoor Growing Tower
heading: Why grow without soil
text: Hydroponics is a way to grow plants without soil. A pH-adjusted water solution carries nutrients straight to the roots, sometimes with an inert medium such as coco coir or rockwool for support. That is the method behind HydroCart.

title: HydroCart Indoor Growing Tower
heading: Why grow without soil
text:
for support. That is the method behind HydroCart.
You can grow indoors year-round, including in winter, because the plants are not tied to field weather ( University of Missouri Extension, 2024 ). Vertical towers also fit in a small indoor footprint, which is useful in a city where outdoor growing space is limited.

title: HydroCart Indoor Growing Tower
heading: Why grow without soil
text:
in a city where outdoor growing space is limited.
Closed or recirculating systems can use water efficiently. In one peer-reviewed comparison of lettuce grown in Yuma, Arizona, hydroponic greenhouse production was estimated at about 20 liters of water per kilogram of lettuce per year, compared with about 250 liters for conventional field lettuce — roughly 13 times less water per kilogram, or about 92% less ( Barbosa et al., 2015 ). Those figures are for that crop and setting, not a promise for every plant in every tower.

The same study found much higher yield per square meter for that hydroponic lettuce, and also much higher energy use per kilogram than field production. Hydroponics is not automatically “low energy,” so we do not claim it is.

Typical hydroponic crops include leafy greens, herbs, tomatoes, peppers, and strawberries. NASA has also tested hydroponic and aeroponic growing without soil on the International Space Station ( NASA XROOTS ).

Can I buy a HydroCart?

What is hydroponics?
Growing plants without soil, with nutrients delivered in water.
Can you grow year-round?
Indoor hydroponic crops can be grown year-round, including in winter, according to University of Missouri Extension.
Does it use less water?

Does it use less water?
Recirculating hydroponic systems can use much less water per kilogram than field growing; a 2015 lettuce study in Arizona estimated about 92% less water per kilogram. Results vary by crop and setup.
Does it use less electricity?
Not necessarily. That same study found much higher energy use per kilogram than field lettuce. We will list HydroCart's measured draw here if we publish one.

title: Terms of Service
heading: Cancellations and refunds
text:
You can cancel at any time. When a project is cancelled, any payment that's waiting is withdrawn and nothing more is due . For stages you've already paid:
Paid, but we haven't started it: full refund of that stage.
In progress: partial refund of that stage, based on the work completed in it when you cancel. We'll explain how we worked it out.
Finished stages: not refundable, because that work has been done.

title: Terms of Service
heading: Free bug fixes for one month
text:
For 30 days after we deploy your project , we'll fix bugs and errors in the work we delivered at no cost. Just email us with your confirmation number and what went wrong.
This covers problems with our work. It doesn't cover new features, changes to the original requirements, or problems caused by changes made by someone else or by third-party services. We're happy to quote those separately.

text: Please give us accurate information and any access we need (for example, accounts or files) to complete your project. Delays in getting these may delay delivery. Don't use our services for anything illegal.

text: Once your project is paid in full, you own the custom work we deliver to you. We keep the right to reuse our general tools, methods and know-how, and to mention the project in our portfolio unless you ask us not to. Third-party software and services stay under their own licenses.
